description: Pineapple Buns, or Bo Lo Bao, are a beloved classic from Hong Kong bakeries, famed for their unique sweet and crispy crust resembling a pineapple's texture. Beneath this delightful topping lies a soft, fluffy milk bread that melts in your mouth. This recipe brings the authentic taste of these iconic buns right to your home kitchen, perfect for breakfast or a sweet snack.

instructions.title: Prepare the Bun Dough
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine 250g all-purpose flour, 30g granulated sugar, 3g instant dry yeast, and 3g salt. Gradually add 120ml warm milk and 1 small beaten egg, mixing until a shaggy dough forms. Knead on a lightly floured surface for 5-7 minutes until smooth. Incorporate 25g softened unsalted butter and knead for another 3-5 minutes until the dough is elastic. Place in a greased bowl, cover, and let rise in a warm place until doubled (approx. 1-1.5 hours, not included in active time).

instructions.title: Make the Pineapple Topping
instructions.text: While the dough is rising, prepare the topping. In a separate bowl, cream 60g softened unsalted butter and 60g granulated sugar until light and fluffy. Beat in 1 large egg yolk until well combined. Sift in 100g all-purpose flour, 10g powdered milk, and 2g baking powder, mixing until a soft dough forms. Wrap in plastic wrap and chill in the refrigerator for at least 15 minutes to firm up (not included in active time).

instructions.title: Shape the Buns
instructions.text: Once the bun dough has doubled in size, gently punch it down to release the air. Divide the dough into 8 equal portions. Roll each portion into a smooth, tight ball. Place the shaped buns on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, leaving ample space between them. Cover loosely and let rise for a second proof for 30-45 minutes (not included in active time).

instructions.title: Form the Pineapple Crust
instructions.text: Remove the chilled topping dough from the refrigerator and divide it into 8 equal portions. On a lightly floured surface or between two pieces of parchment paper, flatten each portion into a thin disc, large enough to cover the top of each proofed bun. Gently place one topping disc over each bun.

instructions.title: Egg Wash and Score
instructions.text: Preheat your oven to 180°C (350°F). Lightly brush the pineapple topping on each bun with the beaten egg wash (using 1 large egg). Using the back of a knife or a dough scraper, gently score a crosshatch pattern on the topping to mimic the texture of a pineapple. Be careful not to cut too deep into the bun itself.

instructions.title: Bake the Pineapple Buns
instructions.text: Place the baking sheet with the prepared buns into the preheated oven. Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until the buns are golden brown and the pineapple topping is crispy and cooked through. Monitor closely to prevent over-browning.

tips: For an extra fluffy bun, ensure your yeast is active and your milk is warm (not hot) to encourage optimal dough rise.
The key to a perfect crispy topping is to work with cold butter for the topping dough. If it gets too soft, chill it again before flattening.
Serve your Pineapple Buns warm, split open with a generous slice of cold butter inserted inside for an authentic Hong Kong cafe experience.
article:
Pineapple Buns, known in Cantonese as Bo Lo Bao (菠蘿包), are a true icon of Hong Kong baking. These golden-domed delights are a staple in bakeries and cha chaan tengs (Hong Kong-style cafes) across Asia and beyond, cherished for their unique combination of textures and irresistible sweetness. If you've ever dreamt of recreating that bakery magic at home, you're in for a treat. Making your own Pineapple Buns is a wonderfully rewarding experience, transforming simple ingredients into a comforting masterpiece. If you're looking for a delightful baking project, mastering the Pineapple Bun Recipe is incredibly rewarding.

## What is Pineapple Bun (Bo Lo Bao)?

Despite its name, the Pineapple Bun contains no actual pineapple fruit. The "pineapple" moniker comes purely from the distinctive appearance of its topping. As the sweet, crumbly crust bakes, it cracks and develops a golden, checkered pattern that resembles the skin of a pineapple. This visual similarity is where the name originates, adding a charming bit of culinary folklore to this beloved pastry.

At its heart, a Pineapple Bun is a sweet, soft, and fluffy bread bun, akin to a brioche or milk bread, crowned with a crisp, sugary, cookie-like crust. The magic lies in this textural contrast: a slightly crunchy, buttery, and sweet topping gives way to a tender, airy bread interior. This combination makes it incredibly satisfying to eat, whether enjoyed plain, with a slab of cold butter, or with a savory or sweet filling. Originating from Hong Kong, Bo Lo Bao has become a quintessential part of its culinary landscape, often enjoyed for breakfast, a snack, or alongside a cup of Hong Kong-style milk tea.

## Ingredients You Need for Pineapple Buns

Crafting the perfect Pineapple Bun involves two distinct components: the soft bread dough and the signature crumbly topping. Using fresh, quality ingredients will make all the difference in achieving that authentic bakery taste and texture.

For the Dough:
*   **Bread Flour (High-Protein Flour):** Essential for a chewy, elastic, and soft crumb.
*   **Granulated Sugar:** Sweetens the dough and aids in browning.
*   **Salt:** Balances the sweetness and enhances flavor.
*   **Instant Yeast:** The leavening agent that makes the bun light and airy.
*   **Warm Milk:** Activates the yeast and provides moisture. Whole milk is recommended for richness.
*   **Large Egg:** Adds richness, color, and helps with structure.
*   **Unsalted Butter (Softened):** Contributes to the tender texture and buttery flavor.

For the Topping (Pineapple Crust):
*   **All-Purpose Flour:** Forms the base of the cookie-like crust.
*   **Granulated Sugar (or Powdered Sugar):** Provides sweetness and contributes to the crisp texture.
*   **Unsalted Butter (Cold, Cubed):** Crucial for achieving that crumbly, shortbread-like consistency. Keeping it cold prevents overmixing.
*   **Large Egg Yolk:** Adds richness, binds the topping, and helps with browning.
*   **Milk or Evaporated Milk (optional):** A tiny splash if the topping mixture is too dry.
*   **Vanilla Extract (optional):** Enhances the sweet aroma.

## Step-by-Step Instructions for Pineapple Bun Recipe

Let's dive into the detailed Pineapple Bun Recipe. This process, while requiring a bit of time for proofing, is straightforward and immensely rewarding.

1.  **Prepare the Dough:**
    *   In a large bowl, whisk together the warm milk and a teaspoon of sugar, then sprinkle in the yeast. Let it sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy, indicating the yeast is active.
    *   In a separate bowl, combine the bread flour, remaining sugar, and salt.
    *   Add the activated yeast mixture and the egg to the dry ingredients. Mix with a spoon or in a stand mixer with a dough hook until a shaggy dough forms.
    *   Knead the dough for about 8-10 minutes until it becomes smooth and elastic. It should pass the "windowpane test" (stretching a small piece thin enough to see light through without tearing).
    *   Gradually add the softened butter, kneading until fully incorporated and the dough is very smooth and elastic, another 5-7 minutes.
    *   Form the dough into a ball, place it in a lightly oiled bowl, cover with plastic wrap, and let it proof in a warm place for 1 to 1.5 hours, or until doubled in size.

2.  **Prepare the Pineapple Topping:**
    *   While the dough is proofing, make the topping. In a medium bowl, cream together the cold, cubed butter and sugar until light and fluffy.
    *   Beat in the egg yolk and vanilla extract (if using) until well combined.
    *   Gradually add the all-purpose flour, mixing until just combined and a crumbly dough forms. Be careful not to overmix. If the mixture is too dry, add a tiny bit of milk.
    *   Form the topping into a disk, wrap it in plastic wrap, and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes to firm up.

3.  **Shape the Buns:**
    *   Once the dough has doubled, gently punch it down to release the air.
    *   Divide the dough into 8-10 equal portions (about 60-70g each). Roll each portion into a smooth ball. Place them on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, leaving space between each.
    *   Take the chilled topping dough and divide it into the same number of portions as your bread dough.
    *   On a lightly floured surface or between two pieces of parchment paper, flatten each portion of topping into a thin disk, large enough to cover the top of your bread dough ball.
    *   Gently place a topping disk over each bread dough ball, pressing lightly to adhere. Use a knife to lightly score a crosshatch pattern on the surface of the topping.

4.  **Second Proofing and Baking:**
    *   Cover the shaped buns loosely with plastic wrap and let them proof again in a warm place for 30-45 minutes, or until visibly puffy (but not doubled).
    *   Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C).
    *   Just before baking, you can brush the exposed edges of the bread dough (not the topping) with a light egg wash (1 egg yolk whisked with 1 tbsp milk) for extra shine.
    *   Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until the topping is golden brown and the buns are cooked through.
    *   Transfer the baked buns to a wire rack to cool slightly.

## Pro Tips for the Best Pineapple Buns

Following this Pineapple Bun Recipe with attention to detail will elevate your results from good to absolutely glorious.

*   **Don't Rush the Kneading:** Proper kneading develops the gluten, which is essential for that signature soft, chewy bread texture. A stand mixer is a huge help here, but manual kneading works too – just be patient!
*   **Perfect Proofing:** The temperature and humidity of your kitchen will affect proofing time. A warm, draft-free spot is ideal. Look for the dough to double in size for the first proof and become visibly puffy for the second. Under-proofed dough will be dense; over-proofed dough can collapse.
*   **Keep the Topping Cold:** The key to a crumbly, shortbread-like topping is using cold butter and not overworking the dough. This prevents the butter from melting prematurely, ensuring a flaky texture. Chill the topping dough well before use.
*   **Gentle Handling:** Once the dough has proofed, handle it gently to avoid deflating all the air you've worked so hard to incorporate.
*   **Scoring is Key:** The crosshatch pattern isn't just for aesthetics; it helps the topping expand and crack beautifully during baking, creating the "pineapple" effect. Don't press too hard, just enough to score the surface.
*   **Eat Them Warm:** Pineapple Buns are undoubtedly best enjoyed fresh from the oven, when the topping is at its crispiest and the bread is at its softest.

## Serving Suggestions for Bo Lo Bao

While the traditional Pineapple Bun Recipe yields a perfect plain bun, Bo Lo Bao is incredibly versatile and can be enjoyed in many delightful ways.

*   **Classic "Bo Lo Yau":** The most iconic way to enjoy a Pineapple Bun is sliced horizontally and filled with a thick slab of cold, unsalted butter. The contrast of the warm, sweet bun with the melting, salty butter is pure heaven.
*   **Breakfast Staple:** Pair it with a cup of strong Hong Kong-style milk tea (nai cha) or coffee for a quintessential Hong Kong breakfast or afternoon tea snack.
*   **Simple Snack:** Enjoy it plain, savoring the unique blend of textures and flavors on its own.
*   **Filled Buns:** Beyond butter, Pineapple Buns are often sold with various fillings. These can include savory options like char siu (BBQ pork), or sweet fillings such as red bean paste, coconut cream, or custard.

## Variations and Substitutions

Experimenting with the basic Pineapple Bun Recipe allows for endless creativity, adapting it to your preferences or dietary needs.

*   **Flavorful Fillings:** Don't limit yourself to just butter. Integrate fillings like a creamy custard, sweet red bean paste, shredded coconut mixed with sugar, or even a savory char siu (BBQ pork) filling for a more substantial meal.
*   **Topping Twists:**
    *   **Chocolate Pineapple Buns:** Add a tablespoon of cocoa powder to the topping mixture for a chocolatey crust.
    *   **Matcha Topping:** Incorporate a teaspoon of matcha powder for an earthy, green tea-infused crust.
    *   **Brown Sugar Topping:** Substitute granulated sugar with light brown sugar for a slightly deeper, caramel-like flavor in the crust.
*   **Dough Enhancements:**
    *   **Richer Dough:** For an even more luxurious bun, increase the butter content in the dough slightly.
    *   **Dairy-Free:** Substitute regular milk with plant-based milk (like almond or soy milk) and use a dairy-free butter alternative for both the dough and topping.
*   **Gluten-Free (Advanced):** Crafting a gluten-free Pineapple Bun Recipe is challenging due to the specific gluten structure required for the bread. However, specialized gluten-free bread flour blends might yield acceptable results, though the texture will differ from the traditional version.

Embrace the joy of home baking and the incredible satisfaction of pulling a tray of warm, fragrant Pineapple Buns from your oven. Embark on your culinary adventure and perfect this beloved Pineapple Bun Recipe. It's a taste of Hong Kong that you can now enjoy anytime, right in your own kitchen!
